the stochastic description is a powerful method for describing the single-particle dynamics of a nuclear system and that it contains an additional coherent damping mechanism that can be interpreted in terms of a coupling between mean-field and single-particle fluctuations.

the stochastic transport description for a single particle in a mean field is a natural extension of the Vlasov equation, and that this stochastic description contains, besides incoherent binary scattering, a coherent damping term which is due to the coupling between mean-field and single-particle fluctuations.

the derivation of stochastic transport equations for the single-parton density matrix and the derivation of the corresponding self-energies for the collective motion.
the development of a stochastic one-body transport theory for the single-parton density matrix.
